title: NWSChat IDSS Update — QLCS Arrival ~22:40

messages.name: McCracken Co EMA
messages.text: Any update on timing for the line? We have our sirens staffed and are holding on opening shelters.

messages.name: NWS Paducah DSS
messages.text: *** EXERCISE EXERCISE EXERCISE — NOT A REAL PRODUCT *** Working on a partner update now. Expect it in about 5 minutes. *** EXERCISE ***

messages.name: NWS Paducah DSS
messages.text: *** EXERCISE EXERCISE EXERCISE — NOT A REAL PRODUCT *** IDSS UPDATE for Brennan County partners. The QLCS is crossing the Tennessee River west of your county now. Line motion is NE at 60 mph (52 kt). KPAH radar loops (SIMULATED CASE DATA) show 2–3 couplets along the leading edge with 0–1 km SRH near 450 m2/s2. Embedded, rain-wrapped tornadoes are LIKELY 22:00–02:00. *** EXERCISE ***

messages.name: NWS Paducah DSS
messages.text: *** EXERCISE *** Best estimate for the leading edge reaching northern Brennan County is ~22:40, give or take 10 minutes. Expect short warning lead times of 5–10 minutes or less on spin-ups. Anyone in manufactured homes should be in a sturdy building BEFORE the line arrives. *** EXERCISE ***

messages.name: NWS Paducah DSS
messages.text: *** EXERCISE *** We remain under PDS Tornado Watch until 04:00. Most tornadoes in this line will be wrapped in heavy rain and will not be visible, especially after dark. Warnings will be RADAR INDICATED first. Treat any tornado warning as the signal to act immediately. *** EXERCISE ***

messages.name: Marshall Co EMA
messages.text: Copy. Is the ~22:40 time for northern Brennan only, or does the whole line arrive then?

messages.name: NWS Paducah DSS
messages.text: *** EXERCISE *** ~22:40 is the leading edge in northern Brennan County, Corwin area. At 60 mph, the rest of Brennan County and then Marshall County follow within roughly 15–30 minutes. Next partner update by 22:05, sooner if we warn. Send spotter reports to us via this room or the EM hotline. *** EXERCISE ***

instructorNote: This core inject sets the clock: the line reaches northern Brennan County around 22:40 and warning lead times may be under 10 minutes, so protective actions, including moving manufactured home residents, have to start now and not wait for a warning. Check that the Warning Officer logs the arrival estimate and confirms Weather Wire, the EAS receiver and NWSChat are receiving, that the EM Director treats 22:40 as the deadline for protective actions under EOP 3.3, and that 911 confirms the Position 2 encoder is ready.
